title: Finite quotient data for a prescribed continuous Galois cocycle
statement: For a field K and the prescribed continuous homogeneous degree-two Galois units cocycle z [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology], its inhomogeneous evaluation c(g,h) [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect] factors as d(q(g),q(h)) through a locally constant homomorphism q to a finite nonempty group Gamma indexed by Fin n. For all g,h in the absolute Galois group and j in Gamma, d(q(g),q(h)j) g(d(q(h),j)) = d(q(g),q(h)) d(q(gh),j). The displayed multiplication on Gamma is its transported group law, not modular multiplication on Fin n. No normalization is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 03R7 surjectivity and Section 0DVG; explicit regular coefficients and finite Galois descent expanded from the parent construction

proof.text: Let G be the absolute Galois group and A the discrete additive form of separable-closure units. Mathlib FieldTheory.Galois.Profinite supplies compactness and local compactness. If f is the homogeneous cochain underlying z, then c(g,h)=f(1,g,gh) is jointly continuous: apply continuous evaluation to the continuous map g ↦ f(1,g) and the continuous multiplication (g,h) ↦ gh.

Apply [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] to the continuous map c on the profinite product group G × G. Obtain an open normal U in G × G under which c is right-invariant. Pull U back along g ↦ (g,1) and g ↦ (1,g), and intersect the two open normal pullbacks to obtain N in G. For a,b in N, both (a,1) and (1,b) belong to U, hence (a,b) belongs to U, so c(ga,hb)=c(g,h). The open quotient G/N is discrete and compact, hence finite. Enumerate it by Fin n and transport its group law using Equiv.group and Equiv.mulEquiv. The quotient is nonempty, so n is nonzero. Compose the quotient homomorphism with the enumeration to obtain a surjective q. The quotient map is continuous into a discrete quotient and therefore locally constant; arbitrary postcomposition preserves local constancy. Choose representatives using the proved surjectivity of q and define d by c on representatives. QuotientGroup.mk'_eq_mk' and the established N-invariance prove that c(g,h)=d(qg,qh). Convert additive values back to units.

The categorical equality iCycles ≫ d = 0 implies that f has zero differential. Evaluate it at (1,g,gh,(gh)r). TopRep.homogeneousCochains.d_apply unfolds this to f(g,gh,ghr)−(f(1,gh,ghr)−(f(1,g,ghr)−f(1,g,gh)))=0. The invariant property of f under diagonal translation gives f(g,gh,g(hr))=g(f(1,h,hr)). Rearrange in the additive coefficient group and apply Additive.toMul to get c(g,h)c(gh,r)=g(c(h,r))c(g,hr). For arbitrary j in Fin n choose r with q(r)=j using surjectivity. Rewrite with the factorization and the homomorphism law q(hr)=q(h)q(r), then commute the two unit factors to get the required identity. No normalization is used.
